findings.title: Missing ecology data falls back silently
findings.description: In `_bake_cell_luts_gd`, a size mismatch in `transition_ages` or `previous_vitalities` sets `has_transition` to false, so each cell silently uses age 0 and its current vitality. No error is logged, and the native encoder in `world_ext_cell_luts.cpp` similarly drops to the cache path when `frame_valid` is false.

citations.citation: Keynes: errors fail loudly instead of falling back silently

evidence.explanation: The fallback `age := transition_ages[ci] if has_transition else 0` hides a length mismatch in data that the commit should always supply, and it does so without `push_error` or an explicit failure.

location.code_snippet:
+		var age := transition_ages[ci] if has_transition else 0
+		var previous_vit := previous_vitalities[ci] if has_transition else cur_vit_byte

findings.title: Held map changes can be dropped
findings.description: `WorldRuntimeDailyAdapter._consume_runtime_commit_if_ready` passes `{}` to `queue_worker_commit` when `authority_ready` is false, and `WorldRuntimeMapUpdates.queue()` interprets that empty commit as a request to clear its latest batch and held dirty and class cells. If earlier tile changes are still held because of the frame budget, they are discarded before encoding while the presented day advances, leaving those textures stale until the cells change again.

citations.citation: Preserve responsive and complete map updates
var whole_graph = bool(report.get("authority_ready", false))

host._presentation.queue_worker_commit(from_day,
			host._runtime_commit_day, host._runtime_commit_generation, commit if whole_graph else {})

evidence.explanation: `whole_graph` comes from `report.authority_ready`, and a false value causes the adapter to pass an empty visual commit. `queue()` takes its `commit.is_empty()` branch and calls `clear_pending()`, erasing `_latest`, `_held_dirty`, and `_held_classes`; `has_pending()` then becomes false, allowing `publish_worker_view` to advance the presented day without applying the held map changes. The existing held-cell test covers only non-empty commits.

location.code_snippet: +			host._runtime_commit_day, host._runtime_commit_generation, commit if whole_graph else {})

findings.title: Real-window frame-rate report covers only the 30 fps setting
findings.description: The alternating real-window table in `feature-status.md` states it re-ran only the 30 fps setting at 50× and tabulates only those rows, while the same section says the pair command runs 30, 60 and adaptive rounds three times each. The 60 fps and adaptive before/after frame-interval P95, sample counts, ranges, background days per second, map updates per second and display lag are therefore not reported anywhere in the PR, even though the 36 regular and 18 injected-load window runs the text cites span all three settings. The report also never says which settings stabilise and which remain limited by drawing cost, so the requested per-setting conclusion is missing.

findings.title: A failed map update freezes the date display
findings.description: `apply_pending_worker_map` returns without clearing the pending update when `publish_worker_climate_visuals` reports no encode path. `publish_worker_view` now refuses to advance while `_map_updates.has_pending()` is true, so after one such failure `simulation_view_updated` never fires again for the rest of the session. That signal drives the time UI and the selected-cell daily lines. The encode reports no path when the baker, sus map or world is missing, or when the LUT dimensions are invalid. It then retries on every frame and never recovers. Before this PR, the view date advanced whatever the outcome of the texture publish.

citations.citation:
func _process(_delta: float) -> void:
	_run_admitted_inline_day()
	_daily_adapter._process(self, _delta)
	_presentation.publish_worker_view(simulation_view_updated.emit)

evidence.explanation: `publish_worker_climate_visuals` returns `{}` when the baker, sus map or last world is null. `refresh_cell_luts_daily` and `bake_cell_luts` return 'none' when the map, world or LUT dimensions are missing. On that path the update is never marked as applied, `has_pending()` stays true, and `publish_worker_view` keeps returning early.

+	if result.get("lut_encode_path", "none") == "none":
+		return

findings.title: Save flush reaches into host internals
findings.description: `_save` in `game_save_coordinator.gd` now reads `_runtime_host._vision_dirty_indices` and calls the host's private `_service_worker_map_presentation` before saving. The save path therefore drives host-owned display state directly rather than through a host-owned intent or committed boundary.

citations.citation: Keynes: cross-module hand-offs go through committed views or intents

evidence.explanation: The save coordinator reads `_runtime_host._vision_dirty_indices` and calls `_service_worker_map_presentation` directly, so another module drives the host's display state and vision dirty list without a public intent.

findings.title: Signal callbacks bypass host binding
findings.description: `_enter_tree` connects `process_frame` and `frame_post_draw` to `_presentation.begin_frame` and `_presentation.observe_draw`, which are the component's own methods rather than host-bound Callables. The matching disconnects in `_exit_tree` depend on those same component-bound references.

citations.citation: Keynes: session components get narrow dependencies and one daily entry

evidence.explanation: The signals are connected to unbound component methods, against the rule that callbacks handed to signals must be Callables bound to the host.

findings.title: Map presenter gets whole host access
findings.description: `apply_pending_worker_map(host, vision_changed)` in the new presentation component takes the entire `WorldRuntimeHost` and writes its fields directly, including `_vision_dirty_indices` and the `_sched_*` and `_dcp_*` timings. This couples the component to host internals instead of narrow Callables or values.

citations.citation: Keynes: session components get narrow dependencies and one daily entry

evidence.explanation: The function reads `host._renderer` and `host._world_clock`, writes `host._vision_dirty_indices`, and updates several host timing fields, so the whole host is passed where narrow dependencies are expected.

findings.title: Post-change window timings are missing
findings.description: The feature status says the after-change real-window run is still pending, and the desktop capture failed to launch Godot. The merged throttling therefore has no alternating before and after samples of frame interval, background days per second, display-update rate or display lag.

findings.title: Launcher exit status hides a failed game run
findings.description: On macOS, `run_sample` takes `result.returncode` from `/usr/bin/open -W`, which reports only whether the app launched, not the Godot process's exit code. A game that crashes after launch therefore passes the `returncode` gate and reaches `load_recording`, where the failure is only inferred from missing or incomplete markers and the recorded `exit_code` in `.run.json` is misleading.

location.code_snippet:
+        with launch_log.open("w") as output:
+            result = subprocess.run(command, stdout=output, stderr=subprocess.STDOUT)
